featured_reviews.name: Ronik
featured_reviews.review_text:
Car itself is fine but sending car for servicing is an headache

At the price point Jeep cars are sold at, one would expect decent, if not excellent, after-sales service. As a owner of a Jeep Compass, I can confidently say that while the car itself is fine, if you’re looking for good after-sales service, do yourself a favor and consider other options or find an alternative service center.
Having owned multiple cars over the years and always opting for authorized service centers, I can say I’ve neverexperienced service this bad. The Jeep Service Centre India has truly set a new low.
Here’s my experience:
On February 28, I arranged a pickup & drop service for a simple tire replacement (all four tires). A straightforward task, right? Instead, they took the entire day. By 8 PM, I got a call stating my car wouldn’t be delivered because the driver for the drop-off service wasn’t available. How is it possible that a tire replacement takes a whole day? Let just give them the doubt of benefit they where extremely busy that day
The next day, the car arrived around 11 AM – 12 PM. Due to work, I couldn’t take delivery at that time. However, when I took my car out on March 2, I was shocked to find there was no fuel in the car! As you can see in the attached image, the fuel gauge was empty, and my car stalled in the middle of the road. I had to push it to the nearest fuel station. Had my car not moved out of the parking lot, I would’ve had to beg to fuel station guy to give me fuel in a bottle (which, by the way, is illegal in India).
Let’s break it down with some numbers:
Before service:
Odometer: 38,008 km
Mileage: 8.6 km/l
Range: 215 km
Fuel: 25 liters (approx.)
After service:
Odometer: 38,055 km
Mileage: 8.6 km/l
Distance traveled: 47 km
Fuel consumption: Approx. 5.5 liters (47 km / 8.6 km/l)
If we factor in another 5 liters for the service center's “contribution,” there should still be 15 liters left in the car. Even if we consider lower mileage, the car should still have 8.2 liters left, providing a range of 33–71 km, depending on driving conditions. This raises a serious concern: Is Jeep Service Centre stealing fuel, or do they simply not care enough to leave us enough to reach a fuel station?
And this isn’t a one-off issue. This happens repeatedly, and I’ve raised it with Jeep Service Centre India, but the response is always the same (there would have been some mistake at your end ; “WE DON’T TOUCH PETROL  THE PETROL IS  CONSUMED BY CAR ITSELF, IF YOU STILL FEEL LIKE WE ARE AT FAULT  WE CAN COMPENSATE YOU RS 500" }. I dont want your compensation, I just want a explanation (where the petrol goes.. ), If not explanation just keep an eyes out for the problem. The lack of communication is appalling. When a part of my car was damaged, it stayed in the service center for over a month. If I hadn’t followed up every 5-7 days, they probably would’ve kept my car for 3–4 months. The friend’s in jeep service centre have a good skill set of ghosting customers.
The pickup and drop service is always late, and even though we are paying for it, I am always left waiting every single time.
It feels like I’m not the customer — they are . They’ve got my money, and they couldn’t care less about providing even the basic level of service.
Jeep India, if you’re serious about retaining customers or expanding further in India, this level of service is unacceptable. If this is the experience your service centres offer, then I’ve lost all trust in the brand.
I know this review would be overshadowed through other mean and no after effect there will be. But still I just want to notify aspiring new car owner.
